subtitle: The production loop, its swappable seams, and the distance between current state and vision.

architectureGroups.subtitle: 3 current · 1 planned

architectureGroups.subtitle: 2 proven implementations
architectureGroups.description: The stable substrate role beneath sandbox lifecycle. Kubernetes and Docker prove that the same boundary has multiple implementations.

architectureGroups.label: Bot capabilities
architectureGroups.subtitle: 1 shipped example, 2 patterns
architectureGroups.description: Reasons to buy rather than architecture peers of the worker or the runner. Each one is a bundle, an eval set, and an operating pattern that rides the isolated runtime. Expand to see the individual capabilities.

architectureGroups.label: Deployed agent
architectureGroups.subtitle: Identity, bundle, deployment
architectureGroups.description: One agent as an install sees it. An agent may be authored elsewhere; what Curie adds is an identity, a bundle it can deploy, and a channel to answer on. Expand to see the three parts.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates explicit namespace adoption
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says there is no adopt flag and an operator must add created-owner labels manually.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI now provides explicit adoption, records the prior namespace contents, and retains the adopted namespace during teardown.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates the live schema assertion
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says rollback has no override when the API pod cannot report its schema.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI accepts an operator-observed live schema revision while still enforcing the compatibility window before Helm mutates the release.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates the quiesce-write fence
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says the worker ignores a refused quiesce write and can strand its owned marker during cleanup.
documentationDrift.current: The worker checks the fenced write result, refuses the stale hook, and clears only the authoritative owned marker.

documentationDrift.title: The trigger catalog predates review, factory issue and cron ingress
documentationDrift.claim: The trigger interface inventories four hardcoded triggers and says every GitHub event other than push or ping is ignored.
documentationDrift.current: The GitHub route admits review feedback and signed labelled factory issues; worker cron claims scheduled slots and enqueues typed turns. The trigger interface has not caught up.

documentationDrift.title: ADRs 0125 and 0126 predate the installation level workspace gate
documentationDrift.claim: The accepted decisions describe a per deployment workspace_enabled value as the runtime capability gate.
documentationDrift.current: The worker deliberately ignores that legacy deployment bit as a coding gate. The worker wide coordinator switch controls availability, while server scoped selection, the repository allowlist, and operator source bindings control workspace authority.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0144 predates the resumable upgrade driver
documentationDrift.claim: The draft records independent lifecycle gates and explicitly says there is no transactional checkpoint or single recovery owner after an earlier combined driver was rejected.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI now resolves and pins a target chart, validates its version and schema metadata before mutation, owns a namespaced checkpoint through resource version compare and set, resumes nine phases, proves exact convergence, runs a target version canary, and records the observed known good version.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0153 describes attachment transport absent from this pin
documentationDrift.claim: The accepted decision describes channel attachment references and a worker transport to the producing adapter, based on implementation outside this repository.
documentationDrift.current: This pin still omits attachments from the channel HTTP input and uses SlackFileClient as the only file transport. The atlas records the accepted direction as planned.

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.subtitle: Surface today
nodes.description: The original production channel. Bolt Socket Mode handles ingress; Slack Web API renders replies, progress cards, and approval cards. It is no longer the only registered production kind.

nodes.label: Discord
nodes.subtitle: Shipped surface
nodes.description: Out-of-process Gateway adapter. Mentions in a bound parent channel create a public thread and placeholder; later thread messages continue the same conversation. v1 supports text, mentions, threads, and streamed edits. It does not implement buttons, DMs, attachments, or interactive approvals, and a Discord failure never falls back to Slack. The adapter now uses the shared telemetry bootstrap and redacting JSON logger for its own package plus discord.py, uvicorn, and httpx. OTLP export is supported, although the adapter still authors no spans or instruments.

nodes.label: Email
nodes.subtitle: Shipped surface
nodes.description: First-party AgentMail adapter. It polls an inbox, posts to POST /channels/turns under a scoped channel token, and sends one threaded reply per turn.completed. Delivery state is local SQLite with one serialized writer. Terminal completion rows compact oldest first under a derived cap without evicting unresolved or leased work, and an oversized database has an offline copy and VACUUM recovery command. Transport failures and all 4xx discovery refusals enter bounded backoff. Provider, channel, and egress credentials may come from per-field existing Secrets without chart ownership of their values. An external collector requires a narrow chart-declared egress peer. It does not implement interactive approvals. The adapter uses shared telemetry and credential redaction, including OTLP export and startup-failure logs, without a generic environment-injection surface. Provider dialing stays within configured egress CIDRs while TLS verifies the provider hostname. Sustained discovery failure makes readiness fail after a bounded interval and appears in status; liveness stays independent and the Service retains reply delivery to the unready adapter.

nodes.label: Teams
nodes.subtitle: Future surface
nodes.description: Named in the vision, but deliberately deferred until a real second channel teaches the adapter interface.

nodes.label: Curie CLI
nodes.subtitle: Agent-facing control
nodes.description: Drives skill, local, and cluster loops. The local/cluster message verbs can replace Slack ingress and reply transport without changing the worker path. Operators can mint and rotate row-scoped channel tokens, while status and doctor expose bounded completion-outbox and mail-delivery health without identifiers. The checkout-only release-accept evaluator reads a private evidence ledger and fails closed unless one unchanged candidate has seven days of accounted canaries and every recovery criterion. Push delivery diagnosis distinguishes configured, reachable, observed, and verified states instead of treating repository binding as delivery proof. A bare curie doctor discovers the platform API from cluster state, cluster up --dev preserves recorded comms and sealing values, and release builds embed the exact source commit used to resolve installer artifacts. Plain cluster up, apply, and diff retain installed typed mail settings, external Secret pairs, paired worker adapter credentials, and installed local inference. Explicit namespace adoption records prior labels and objects, and cluster down retains the adopted namespace. Hosted connector deploys wait for current revision readiness; skill and local connector startup share one configurable bounded deadline. Explicit source decisions take precedence without replaying stale inline credentials. Offline dry-run plans do not read an installed release. Cluster up and apply wait for the installed Helm target workloads to converge; cluster status returns failure with redacted generation, replica, image and hook diagnoses when the target is unhealthy. Cluster upgrade resolves the selected release chart or explicit local/ref target, pins it to the requested version, validates declared chart version and rendered target schema metadata before mutation, and requires explicit forward-only admission for pending contract or irreversible migrations. One namespaced ConfigMap owns the operation and its durable nine-phase checkpoint through resourceVersion and holder compare-and-set. A resumed upgrade proves exact target images, generations, replicas, hooks, queues, and manifest state, then runs a target-version canary and records known-good from the observed release version. The CLI rollback catalog for v0.9.0 spans migrations 0001 through 0044; it is distinct from the API image serving compatibility window of 0044 through 0044. The 0.9.2 and 0.9.3 release identities each carry the exact 0045 through 0045 schema window because no migration landed between them. CI refuses a new migration unless the release windows advance consistently. The restore and upgrade drills exercise stable installation survival and recovery. Sibling tag image reports require a unique serving Node inventory binding and conditional Node read; this does not prove mutable tag freshness. An explicit cluster context pins every Helm and kubectl child. Channel token operations refuse failed release discovery instead of guessing a Secret name. Retained up escapes literal dotted object keys, while upgrade preserves scalar types through JSON values. Ambiguous 0.8.8 and 0.8.9 rollback identities require retained schema metadata. Local commands and ladder runs honor explicit Compose project and endpoint settings.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.subtitle: Push / PR trigger
nodes.description: Webhook and outbound commit polling converge on the API git-flow engine. Dev pushes build and evaluate; production pushes promote. Repository binding is not delivery proof: pushes arrive through either an operator-created webhook or configured commit polling, and Curie reports only observed configuration rather than claiming that exposure proves delivery. The platform also clones managed workspaces and publishes through an approval-gated path that never leaves write credentials inside the sandbox. One scoped thread and repository own one fenced pull request lineage. Human issue comments, pull request review comments, and submitted reviews are admitted only for the currently open bound pull request after fresh provider reads confirm the immutable repository, installation, pull request, binding generation, and exact head. Accepted feedback enters a durable outbox for the original scoped thread; stale heads, terminal pull requests, unavailable provider truth, and authority mismatches start no model turn. Signed labelled issue events now admit one canonical factory WorkItem, while relabel, unlabel, issue comments, and review events retain distinct authority checks. Factory status and final outcome comments use the GitHub issue as their operator surface.

nodes.label: External hook
nodes.subtitle: HMAC-triggered turn
nodes.description: A named, HMAC-authenticated API hook creates a quota- and body-bounded webhook-sourced turn whose authenticated payload is escaped and delimited as untrusted prompt content. For alert-driven coding, an operator-owned source binding extracts a configured workload fact and maps it to an allowlisted repository plus recorded revision. Missing, ambiguous, malformed, or unauthorized mappings refuse before workspace selection, and payload URLs never choose the target. Bundle-declared hook lifecycle and schedules remain planned.

nodes.label: Console UI
nodes.subtitle: Operations surface
nodes.description: A real API-backed console for fleet, runs, metrics, cost, logs, versions, evals, approvals, and memory. Approval resolution uses the authenticated Console session subject rather than a caller-supplied actor. Usage and Settings remain honest stubs. An external API requires an explicit proxy target; chart rendering refuses a disabled in-chart API without that target.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.subtitle: Ingress · dedupe · placeholder
nodes.description: Before Socket Mode, a bounded startup preflight waits for API health and verifies configured Slack destination capabilities. The live dispatcher then normalizes Slack events and Block Kit text into QueuedTurn, carries adapter scoped file references without downloading their bytes, records adapter owned refusals, deduplicates ingress, posts the placeholder, and appends to the run stream. Bot authored thread messages are admitted only for explicitly trusted bot and channel pairs. Approval clicks become independently signed, approval bound chat principal attestations; an exact record miss is treated as another release owning that approval, never as authority to mutate it. Its single Deployment replica uses a Recreate rollout so Socket Mode never runs two clients on one app token; Slack retries delivery across the reconnect gap.

nodes.label: Port adapter service
nodes.subtitle: Third-party channel edge
nodes.description: The accepted placement for a generic third-party adapter kit: a deployed service, not a bundle-loaded plugin. Slack, Discord, and email already ship as first-party surfaces. The generic adapter manifest, install flow, service discovery, and conformance kit remain unbuilt.

nodes.label: Channel HTTP edge
nodes.subtitle: Generic ingress + egress
nodes.description: The API mints row-scoped channel tokens and platform-owned QueuedTurn records; every mint increments the row generation before signing, so reminting immediately revokes the prior token. A separately scoped adapter principal can rotate its own credential, mint channel tokens only for bindings it serves, list approvals on those routes, and resolve eligible explicit-user approvals. Discord and email already consume this HTTP edge. Worker-side HttpReplyAdapter posts the four versioned reply events to each binding's server-controlled endpoint, while the reserved built-in cluster-message relay returns CLI-driven replies through the API.

nodes.label: API
nodes.subtitle: Control plane · git flow
nodes.description: Owns agents, versions, deployments, multi-surface channel bindings, approvals, state, connector rendering, managed repository workspaces, bundle validation, git flow deploys, and read proxies. Scoped thread workspace identity, one active thread and repository pull request lineage, publication revision reservations, GitHub review authority, delivery audit, and the durable feedback outbox are control-plane state. Source bindings let operators map alert workload facts to an allowlisted repository and recorded revision without trusting payload URLs. Bundle archive validation runs outside the API event loop. Readiness exercises the same list agents query as the public endpoint, while liveness stays process local, so a database state that breaks normal reads removes the pod from service without restarting it. The v0.10.0 API image declares its serving schema window separately from the CLI release catalog. A version cannot become live when its bundle declares an approval route that the agent has not bound, and a live binding cannot be removed underneath that declaration. Approval resolution authenticates chat, Console, operator, or scoped adapter principals; the platform key alone cannot resolve. An opt-in break-glass route can report approval identity gaps and reject a stranded approval with an atomic audit entry and ordinary resume event. Transcript value and namespace capacity refusals increment bounded counters while readiness remains independent of data capacity. Signed factory issue intake, durable WorkItems and ExecutionRequests, a leased status comment outbox, observed CI state, explicit publication policy, and outcome routes are API owned. Per thread transcripts moved from the shared state namespace to a dedicated capped table with terminal and idle expiry.

nodes.label: Valkey streams
nodes.subtitle: Runs · evals · delivery
nodes.description: At-least-once streams carry run and eval jobs. Shared consumer machinery provides bounded delivery, a renewable fenced owner per delivery, lease-expiry recovery, and dead-letter handling. Conversation locks are stamped with consumer ownership and can transfer only after capability plus sustained missing-alive proof. The same bounded graveyard also retains terminal completion-outbox failures, which are not replayable inbound entries. An external Valkey can require TLS; one shared chart helper keeps all seven consumers on the same transport and refuses TLS for the in-chart broker without a TLS listener.

nodes.label: Worker kernel
nodes.subtitle: Route · claim · steer · recover
nodes.description: The concurrency hub: resolves the active deployment, emits a typed terminal failure instead of dropping turns when none exists, enforces one live session per scoped conversation, selects steer versus fresh turn, and protects side effects. It resolves channel attachment references, stores accepted files under a private prefix, and issues a short lived signed redemption reference before claiming the sandbox. Managed coding uses the canonical scoped thread identity rather than a bare reply id. The worker selects and sanitizes an allowlisted repository checkout, archives it privately, and swaps a late workspace into the route only at a fenced turn boundary; multiple ambiguous bare owner/repo-like tokens leave repository selection absent, while multiple explicit repository URLs are refused. Review turns never steer a live sandbox: fresh authority is verified again, the exact accepted pull request head is reserved and materialized, and a replacement sandbox cold-claims that checkout. Publication validates a revision against its base, captures the immutable GitHub repository, installation, and pull request node identities in the same write that opens the pull request, creates a fresh approval, and reconciles approved work through the same pull request lineage; stale, terminal, unavailable, or mismatched authority is refused before model or write work. Runs, evals, kill switch, heartbeat, connector, publication, and completion loops are individually supervised with exponential backoff; a repeatedly crashing loop is parked after a bounded streak while siblings continue. Terminal reply events enter a durable, generation fenced completion outbox before the done marker; independent bounded sweeps retry delivery and quarantine expired or malformed records. Each runner request is capped by both the configured runner ceiling and the delivery's remaining deadline. Upgrade drain refuses a fenced quiesce write. Runner error classifications are allowlisted across runner and worker; escalation detail is redacted before it reaches either the user reply or logs. Generic turns still execute with repository workspaces disabled; named repository requests, verified review feedback, and retained repository sessions refuse before execution. Retained generic attachment turns replace only an authenticated idle runner with durable history through an exact claim and generation fence. Repository attachment replacement remains deferred. One bounded idle route reclamation follows a proven ResourceQuota refusal and retries only after exact quota headroom is observed. The effective runner timeout bounds the whole stream; unconfirmed timeout ownership ends terminally instead of retrying. The factory dispatcher acquires durable requests before starting a turn, waits on capacity, reconciles orphaned runs, observes cancellation, and rotates CI repair rounds without losing the WorkItem. A declared cron trigger is claimed once per slot in SQL and enqueued onto the same bounded run stream. Factory execution is capped by its three hour deadline and an explicit turn budget.

nodes.label: Approval plane
nodes.subtitle: Durable human gate
nodes.description: A gate terminates the turn as AWAITING_APPROVAL, persists a durable record and its validated originating trace context, suspends the sandbox, and later resumes through a new queued resolution turn that continues that trace when available. The runner's PreToolUse hook is the primary permission gate and can_use_tool is its backstop. Configuration-time checks refuse a declared-but-unbound approval route before deployment or route mutation, while request-time checks remain the fail-safe. Legacy or malformed carriers intentionally start a clean root. The resume reconciler's grace is derived from the delivery budget plus shutdown reserve. Resolution accepts only authenticated chat, Console, operator, or scoped adapter principals and checks every principal, including the requester, against the captured approver set. An adapter can see and resolve only approvals served by its binding set, and only through explicit user routes. When multiple releases share one Slack app, only the API owning the approval record may resolve it. One resolution target owns the sole interactive card. An optional pager target receives text only, with no ConfirmIntent, action value, or remembered card reference, so it cannot create a second approval card or authority path. Publication approval is fresh for each proposed revision, never resumes the model directly, and review feedback is not itself an approval. Known read-only tools avoid approval and receipt side effects. Durable authority is recorded before any card or notice delivery, including turns without an existing reply reference. Publication cards preserve the CLI reply adapter and a stable pending lifetime. The shipped SRE gates, including mcp__curie__publish_changes, carry sre-approvals; explicit user bindings allow operator resolution without Slack transport. A separately granted administrative recovery path can reject and audit a stranded approval without widening the ordinary membership decision.

nodes.label: Eval plane
nodes.subtitle: Cases · graders · report
nodes.description: The same bundle-carried eval suite runs across skill, local, local-release, and cluster. Worker scores and records cases, then reports a rollup to the API.

nodes.label: Sandbox
nodes.subtitle: One isolated session
nodes.description: An isolated runtime claimed per conversation. Kubernetes Agent Sandbox is production; Docker runs the same image locally. Accepted inbound files appear read only under /attachments on both substrates. Managed repository content appears at /workspace from a private signed one-object reference and digest; GitHub and object-store credentials never enter the runner. Kubernetes redeems references in dedicated credentialless init containers, while Docker redeems them in the substrate driver. A late workspace or accepted review replaces the route only at a fenced turn boundary, and review work starts from the exact verified pull request head in a newly claimed sandbox. Session identity can arrive over the ACI so a warm pool sandbox may be prebound before the turn. Chart render fails closed if the retired in path LiteLLM sidecar is reenabled (ADR-0037). Retained attachment replacement preserves the logical session and transcript while cold creating a candidate before detaching the old route. Capacity, binding, or fence failure preserves the old claim. Quota pressure can reclaim at most one safe idle route and does not add a background scheduler.

nodes.label: Runner / ACI server
nodes.subtitle: Multi-turn session loop
nodes.description: Serves event, steer, interrupt, timeout, reset, and snapshot; translates harness events into the frozen NDJSON union; injects memory and history; and probes MCP capabilities conservatively. For hosted Bearer connectors, the runner expands the named secret into the in memory MCP header, removes that name from the process environment, and writes the full MCP configuration to a mode 0600 file instead of the Claude process argv. Missing or empty credentials still halt before a model call with a names only diagnosis. A failed capability probe is retried inside each later accepted turn; a persistent probe failure denies that connector's tools and reports the condition while still running the model. The disallowed tool list blocks named tools rather than the underlying credential backed capability. Permission enforcement layers a primary PreToolUse hook with a can_use_tool backstop, and runner local disallowed tool policy applies to both real and fake sessions. Bundle command hooks run from the mounted plugin root with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT set; exit 2 denies, while exit 0 stdout can return a deny, ask, or stop decision. Telemetry records each observed provider wait and tool wait interval as root siblings with bounded phase, terminal, round, TTFT, and outcome attributes. Portable structured history preserves ordered messages and tool results, with optional native checkpoints for cache reuse. Appends reserve room for durable publication outcomes. On a capacity refusal the runner compacts through versioned compare-and-set, preserves publication markers and the newest turn, reloads on conflicts, and retries. Only a capacity refusal that survives bounded compaction replaces success or approval with history-persistence-error and CLASSIFIED_FAILURE; ordinary append failures retain the outcome but mark durability lost. Boot uses the same bounded compaction and reload path before accepting a turn.

nodes.label: Claude harness
nodes.subtitle: Declared package today
nodes.description: The only production harness contribution. ModelSession exists, but raw SDK messages and the Claude Code plugin format still cross the conceptual boundary. Draft ADR-0140 would stop the speculative multi-harness program until a real second engine exists; while Draft, it authorizes no change to the accepted harness contracts.

nodes.label: Model endpoint
nodes.subtitle: Provider-selected inference
nodes.description: Anthropic is the default; OpenRouter, Zhipu, Moonshot, DeepSeek, and opt-in Ollama routes are also built. Cluster Ollama pulls now require an explicit durable-storage policy or a declaration that weights are pre-provisioned; ephemeral implicit downloads are refused before mutation. Native OpenAI wire format remains absent.

nodes.label: MCP connector hosts
nodes.subtitle: Collapsed MCP implementations
nodes.description: Bundle declared hosted, source built, remote, and unhosted fallback MCP implementations remain collapsed behind this role. Cluster deploy waits for each hosted Deployment's current revision to become ready or fails with a bounded redacted diagnosis. Skill and local startup use a separate Docker host outside the connector port and share one configurable bounded readiness deadline. The platform separately warns when a hosted workload has no mounted MCP entry. Runner boot performs the actual MCP capability and authentication probe, then later turns may retry a transient probe failure without redialing missing credentials. Renderer and CLI now share a frozen derived Bearer selection rule. Draft ADR-0158 documents a bundle-built HTTP MCP server that owns its provider credential, based on retained historical spike evidence, but it authorizes no new product surface.

nodes.label: MCP OAuth gateway
nodes.subtitle: Per-person delegated access
nodes.description: The accepted vision boundary for delegated MCP authorization. The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted tokens, refresh, revocation, and grants; the gateway applies the active run principal's grant without exposing raw OAuth tokens to the runner.

nodes.label: Agent Proxy
nodes.subtitle: Credentials + egress boundary
nodes.description: Accepted architecture moves provider credentials and enforceable egress policy out of the sandbox. The direction is decided, but substrate, TLS termination, credential injection, and implementation remain follow-up work.

nodes.label: OTel collector
nodes.subtitle: Telemetry write port
nodes.description: Receives OTLP from Curie services and the runner and exports to Langfuse over HTTP. Ingress, durable approval resolution, expiry, and reconciliation preserve the originating W3C trace context when valid; missing or malformed legacy carriers start clean roots. Request path operation spans may carry curie.channel.event_id from a task local scope, while metrics reject that unbounded identifier and maintenance work outside the request scope remains unstamped. The runner emits truthful sibling provider and tool phase intervals with a closed versioned attribute set; the collector boundary remains mostly vendor neutral. Chart CI discovers first party workloads from rendered images and rejects a new workload without the shared OTLP environment. Discord independently bootstraps the same telemetry package outside the chart. Provider teardown shares one wall clock deadline, and supervised worker restarts have bounded restart and give up outcomes. For chart managed sandboxes with NetworkPolicy enabled, a configured external collector endpoint requires declared runner egress CIDRs; chart rendering refuses an undeclared route. Disabling telemetry requires no collector egress rule.

nodes.label: Langfuse
nodes.subtitle: Traces · metrics · eval scores
nodes.description: The current trace and eval store. The shipping Helm surface pins the reviewed Langfuse web and worker migration set together with ClickHouse 25.12.11.4, avoiding an upstream-republished minor alias; its AVX preflight fails the default installation on AVX-less nodes rather than allowing a migration-incompatible store. Compose retains its separate SSE4.2-safe ClickHouse pin for local evidence. The API reconstructs trees and metrics through a vendor-specific read adapter. Operators can disable the in-chart deployment and point every consumer at an explicit external Langfuse host without rendering a nonexistent in-cluster Service. External Langfuse and ClickHouse endpoints use validated HTTP or HTTPS scheme settings shared by their chart consumers. Observation trees expose toolName from the recorded tool span attribute so a consumer can identify the concrete tool executed.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.subtitle: Control-plane state
nodes.description: Stores agents, versions, deployments, channel bindings, approvals, memory, WorkItems, ExecutionRequests, hook runs, factory status and outcome state, and per thread transcripts. Migrations 0040 through 0056 add scoped publication and review authority, operator source bindings, factory admission and dispatch, cron slots, publication policy, tenant groundwork, isolated transcripts, cancellation, execution deadlines, and status comments. Database constraints and compare and set versions fence competing publication, review, and factory work.

nodes.label: RustFS / S3
nodes.subtitle: Immutable bundles
nodes.description: Stores immutable agent bundles, eval inputs, managed workspaces, and inbound attachment bytes over an S3 compatible service. The API ObjectStore, worker BundleReader, and worker WorkspaceObjectPort are three distinct adapter surfaces. Attachment materialization additionally requires streaming operations and presigned reads. With a bring your own store and egress rail enabled, runner bundle fetch is fail closed until explicit store CIDRs and ports are supplied; the key free path also requires separate STS egress and uses projected service account identity rather than node metadata.

nodes.label: Kubernetes
nodes.subtitle: Production substrate
nodes.description: Baseline production substrate: platform services, Agent Sandbox CRDs, security rails, connector workloads, and observability dependencies. A canonical external values profile disables the four chart owned backing stores and points consumers at operator supplied endpoints and Secrets. Helm upgrades preserve external credential references and heal missing or blank legacy chart managed Secret keys while retaining nonblank persisted values. Explicit adoption records a separate label pair and is retained on teardown. Runner API and OTLP egress rails key from the effective endpoint, including extra environment overrides, and fail closed without narrow peers. Connector and general runner egress entries require concrete ports and refuse metadata covering ranges or ineffective exceptions. Mail's external collector path has the same explicit peer requirement. In fake mode the worker and runner receive no live model credential, and an inference weights PVC with the keep annotation survives removal of the local model workload. Chart rendering rejects duplicate reserved environment variables; upgrade drains and digest pinned prewarm bundle fetch images are tied to the candidate generation, and BYO Postgres security probes omit an in chart endpoint they cannot reach.

nodes.label: Docker
nodes.subtitle: Local parity substrate
nodes.description: Runs the same worker and runner image locally behind the same SandboxClient contract.

nodes.label: Dark Factory
nodes.subtitle: Operating pattern
nodes.description: A shipped single agent bundle and durable platform loop for one labelled GitHub issue and one pull request. Signed issue intake admits a WorkItem, SQL owns waiting and execution identity, the worker claims an isolated sandbox, and an explicitly configured automatic publication policy can open or revise the same pull request. Status comments, cancellation, worker loss recovery, bounded three hour runs, CI wait and repair rounds, and outcome reads are part of this operating pattern. The platform records state and evidence; the bundle owns correctness judgments.

nodes.label: Chief of Staff
nodes.subtitle: Operating pattern
nodes.description: A scheduled briefing pattern that reads across sources on a fixed cadence and posts one digest to a channel. It is a bundle plus a schedule plus a channel binding, not a new architecture box.

nodes.label: SRE triage
nodes.subtitle: Example bundle
nodes.description: A shipped example bundle that triages alerts, gathers Kubernetes evidence, and gates mutations through approval routes. Its default credential limits writes to demo workloads. An optional, operator applied grant expands that same connector across built in resources while keeping Secret reads blocked; approval remains the checkpoint for writes, but the connector credential itself carries the wider Kubernetes authority. This is a bundle policy choice within the isolated runtime.

nodes.label: Agent identity
nodes.subtitle: Who the agent is
nodes.description: The agent record and its principal: the name a channel binds to, the credentials it may use, and the approval routes that answer for it. Identity is what Curie supplies to an agent that was authored anywhere else. Accepted ADR-0155 fixes the future tenant, human principal, provider installation, bot identity, release, and installation vocabulary, Its tenant schema groundwork has landed, while the broader identity and enforcement stages remain incomplete.

nodes.label: Agent bundle
nodes.subtitle: What it knows
nodes.description: The versioned bundle that carries the agent prompt, skills, tool policy, and connector declarations. It is the unit that moves between installs.

nodes.label: Agent deployment
nodes.subtitle: Where it runs
nodes.description: The active deployment of a bundle in one install: the sandbox template, the substrate it claims, and the channel it answers on. Replacing the deployment is how an agent is upgraded.

seams.label: Channel ingress + binding
seams.implementations: 3 production channels (Slack Bolt, Discord HTTP adapter, email HTTP adapter), a built-in cluster-message reply relay, plus the CLI transport stub
seams.contract: QueuedTurn + ReplyHandle; neutral {kind, address} deployment binding; adapter scoped Attachment references
seams.reason: Slack, Discord, and email all mint or consume the same channel neutral QueuedTurn and (kind, address) binding. Discord and email prove the HTTP edge that Slack does not use, every adapter token remint rotates its row generation, and the reserved built-in cluster-message relay provides the third ReplySink implementation for CLI-driven turns. Slack additionally proves that file references can cross ingress without putting bytes or URLs on the wire.
seams.leakage: Discord v1 and email do not share Slack's in process dispatcher or approval cards; exact address validation remains Slack specific while other kinds use the generic nonempty rule. SlackFileClient is the only AttachmentFilePort implementation, is wired regardless of channel kind, and requires Slack files:read even though other adapters simply emit no attachments today.
seams.nextStep: Let another channel's concrete interaction and address needs teach the next shared contract instead of speculating beyond the three shipped adapters. ADR 0153 accepts adapter attachment transport, but this pin still has no channel HTTP attachment input or non Slack file transport.

seams.label: Reply delivery semantics
seams.implementations: SlackReplyAdapter plus HttpReplyAdapter consumed by Discord and email
seams.contract: ReplySink.emit over turn.status, reply.update, reply.post, and turn.completed
seams.reason: The four versioned reply events now leave the worker for three surfaces. Slack still owns edit-in-place streaming and approval-card settlement.
seams.leakage: Discord v1 falls back to text and does not implement buttons. Email sends one correspondent-visible reply per turn.completed and does not settle approvals. Neither surface may fall back to Slack.
seams.nextStep: Keep the HTTP reply wire; add Discord interaction or treat email's one-shot reply as a distinct delivery policy rather than a missing Slack feature.

seams.label: Semantic channel interaction
seams.implementations: 2 real renderers (Slack Block Kit, terminal selector)
seams.contract: Versioned OutboundMessage with text fallback, Choice, Confirm, and semantic action values
seams.reason: Two distinct surfaces render the same semantic message without putting their widgets in the contract.
seams.leakage: The terminal mirror is handwritten and capabilities are modeled but not dynamically negotiated. Discord and email do not render Choice or Confirm.
seams.nextStep: Wire capability negotiation when a shipped surface other than Slack needs buttons or cards.

seams.label: Queue / stream broker
seams.implementations: 1 real broker (Valkey) behind producer and consumer ports
seams.contract: StreamPublisher + StreamBroker ports, frozen payload field, shared bounded consumer, one renewable fenced owner per delivery, and an independently retried terminal completion outbox
seams.reason: The port and consumer invariants are explicit, but a second broker has not exercised them.
seams.leakage: Some API producers and graveyard readers still bypass the ports; the completion outbox is another off-port writer to the shared graveyard. Conversation lock ownership, liveness records, token checked Lua, set verbs, and redis-py exception types also leak Valkey semantics.
seams.nextStep: No speculative adapter; promote only if a real broker demand appears.

seams.label: Sandbox substrate
seams.implementations: 2 real implementations (Kubernetes, Docker)
seams.contract: Seven method SandboxClient lifecycle with bounded request deadlines, complete quota rejection evidence, and quota_has_headroom
seams.reason: The same kernel and runner operate through two materially different runtime implementations.
seams.leakage: SandboxView.port, model credential forwarding, connector secret delivery, warm pool behavior, attachment redemption, and production capacity still differ across Kubernetes and Docker. Docker redeems and bind mounts accepted files in the substrate driver; Kubernetes gives the signed reference only to an init container and keeps it off the runner. Kubernetes proves exact named ResourceQuota headroom before one requester retry; Docker cannot prove Kubernetes quota state and returns false. Retained attachment replacement temporarily needs capacity for two claims.
seams.nextStep: Keep parity tests focused on the shared outcomes; do not turn substrate choice into a product axis.

seams.label: Cluster lifecycle admission
seams.implementations: 1 Helm and kubectl lifecycle coordinated by the Rust CLI with a worker pre-upgrade hook
seams.contract: Resolve and pin target chart; validate target version, configuration, and schema metadata; own one namespaced CAS checkpoint; drain, migrate once, apply, converge, canary, and commit observed known-good state
seams.reason: The resumable nine-phase driver now owns one namespaced ConfigMap through resourceVersion and holder tests while the pre-upgrade hook keeps installation-scoped drain authority. Retained configuration preserves scalar types and literal dotted keys, explicit context selection binds all child processes to one cluster, and the v0.9.2 release window validates schema 0045 independently of the development head. Pending approvals have a versioned additive v2.2 identity shape plus an audited opt-in recovery path for upgrades that strand old rows.
seams.leakage: Helm, kubectl, rendered chart metadata, worker drain state, approval identity migration fences, and the target API's serving window remain concrete dependencies. The checkpoint is a durable recovery owner, not a general distributed transaction across Helm and Kubernetes.
seams.nextStep: Use release upgrade and interruption drills to harden recovery without adding a second lifecycle implementation prematurely.

seams.label: Frozen ACI protocol
seams.implementations: 1 production producer + scripted reference/conformance implementation
seams.contract: SessionConfig, boot env, HTTP control verbs, versioned NDJSON events, and normalized ErrorEvent classification across Python, TypeScript, and Rust
seams.reason: This is the strongest documented boundary, and runner and worker now normalize error classifications through shared vectors, but only one production harness stack has proven it end to end.
seams.leakage: A non-Claude harness must still consume or translate the Claude Code plugin bundle shape.
seams.nextStep: Use the conformance guide against a genuinely different production harness.

seams.label: Runner ↔ harness / ModelSession
seams.implementations: 1 production SDK + fake
seams.contract: In-process ModelSession protocol and declared harness contribution
seams.reason: The named protocol is real, but its message union is still SDK-shaped and the bundle distribution format is Claude Code verbatim.
seams.leakage: A foreign harness must emit Claude SDK-shaped objects or replace the runner adapter while also interpreting the Claude plugin format.
seams.nextStep: Prove the out-of-process ACI boundary with a second harness; keep provider-native checkpointing an optional capability.

seams.label: Declared harness package
seams.implementations: 1 declared contribution (Claude)
seams.contract: HarnessContribution manifest; built-ins resolve directly and third-party contributions use curie.harness entry points
seams.reason: Selection and declared assets are clean, but there is no second real package and third-party conformance remains unproven.
seams.leakage: The registry currently wraps the same built-in adapter rather than demonstrating substitution.
seams.nextStep: Publish and run contribution conformance against a non-built-in package.

seams.label: Model provider + credentials
seams.implementations: Multiple live endpoints through one Claude-SDK / Anthropic-wire strategy
seams.contract: Declared wire protocol, provider endpoint, canonical credential keys, and boot-env forwarding
seams.reason: Several endpoints exercise routing and credential resolution, but they do not represent multiple independent provider or harness implementations of the boundary.
seams.leakage: Native OpenAI wire format is absent; several providers share compatibility routing rather than independent harness implementations.
seams.nextStep: Add native OpenAI wire only when its semantics are tested through the live-provider parity tier.

seams.label: Telemetry / OTLP
seams.implementations: 1 trace backend (Langfuse) behind an OTel collector
seams.contract: OTLP write path + versioned phase semantics + Curie API DTO read path
seams.reason: Curie preserves valid W3C parentage from ingress through durable approval resolution, expiry, and reconciliation. Request path operation spans may carry a task local channel event id without widening metric cardinality. The runner records real provider and tool intervals, Discord uses the shared bootstrap, chart CI discovers instrumented workloads, provider shutdown shares one deadline, and supervised restarts emit bounded restart and give up outcomes. Only Langfuse has exercised both sides. Transcript capacity produces bounded value and namespace failure counters, and observation trees preserve concrete tool identity.
seams.leakage: Vendor attributes and /langfuse URL namespaces still leak into the otherwise neutral boundary; the read adapter spans multiple modules.
seams.nextStep: Map vendor span attributes in the collector and neutralize read-route naming.

seams.label: Eval case + scorer
seams.implementations: Multiple grader kinds plus a trajectory matcher across Python and Rust
seams.contract: Frozen eval-case schema + shared trajectory vectors + tri-state outcomes
seams.reason: Distinct scoring implementations and two languages exercise the case boundary, with shared fixtures pinning semantics.
seams.leakage: Python and Rust still implement graders separately; cluster answer-quality failure is not yet universally fatal.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance verification before making cluster answer-quality promotion fatal.

seams.label: Eval result store
seams.implementations: 1 backend (Langfuse traces + scores)
seams.contract: Eval recorder write + EvalMatrix read DTO + version:/suite: tag convention
seams.reason: The platform owns the result shape, but only one backend and one unfrozen tag convention have exercised it.
seams.leakage: The recorder and matrix reader encode Langfuse tags and API behavior directly.
seams.nextStep: Record or freeze the tag convention; wait for a real second store before inventing a generic adapter.

seams.label: Blob storage
seams.implementations: 1 backend (RustFS) over S3-compatible protocol
seams.contract: API ObjectStore + worker BundleReader + worker WorkspaceObjectPort + bundle, attachment, and managed workspace init paths
seams.reason: The port is explicit and S3-compatible services are configuration swaps, but no non-S3 implementation has tested the abstraction.
seams.leakage: API and worker use three separate adapter surfaces. Workspace and attachment operations additionally require streaming put and get, delete, list, and presigned reads. Bucket bootstrap, init containers, migration, key free auth, and NetworkPolicy CIDR configuration retain S3 specific obligations.
seams.nextStep: Leave it alone until a real non-S3 demand appears; keep the BYO egress and web-identity render assertions as the fail-closed operational boundary.

seams.label: Relational database
seams.implementations: 1 engine family (Postgres; self-hosted or managed)
seams.contract: SQLAlchemy models + Alembic migrations + DSN, including scoped workspace identity, fenced pull request lineage, immutable GitHub identity, revision reservations, review audit, adapter principal audit, and durable outbox rows
seams.reason: Managed Postgres is a clean operational swap, but another SQL engine has not exercised the model boundary.
seams.leakage: Postgres UUID, JSONB, schema qualification, native enums, DISTINCT ON SQL, asyncpg-specific JSONB decoding, PostgreSQL 15 NULLS NOT DISTINCT workflow-state identity, partial unique indexes for active publication ownership, and database constraints for one active lineage and reservation ownership remain in application code or migrations.
seams.nextStep: Keep Postgres opinionated unless a concrete alternate engine demand emerges.

seams.label: Approval authorizer
seams.implementations: 3 real approver sets (channel, user group, explicit users)
seams.contract: ApproverSet / ApprovalCreator + authenticated ApprovalPrincipal + durable semantic approval record, with one interactive resolution card, a fresh publication approval for each revision, and a separately granted audited recovery path
seams.reason: Three distinct membership strategies exercise one API-owned authorization interface after resolver identity is authenticated separately. Chat, Console, operator, and adapter credentials all derive server-owned principal facts before that common decision. The shipped SRE publication gate carries its policy route, enabling explicit user operator resolution; durable rows precede transport delivery.
seams.leakage: Channel membership remains Slack-shaped, while Console, operator, and adapter principals are intentionally eligible for only the approver sets their credential kind can satisfy. The administrative recovery route deliberately bypasses ordinary membership only when its installation grant is enabled and writes an atomic audit entry. Publication approvals settle durable publication state rather than resuming a model turn, and optional pager delivery is text only.
seams.nextStep: Exercise the scoped adapter principal through another interactive channel before broadening approval authority.

seams.label: Approval principal identity
seams.implementations: 4 authenticated principal kinds (chat, Console, operator, adapter)
seams.contract: Canonical ApprovalPrincipal + credential-kind eligibility + authenticated audit fields
seams.reason: Four independent credential paths derive one server-owned principal shape before the common membership decision. The adapter credential is bound to a subject, a nonempty set of channel bindings, three exact scopes, and a bounded expiry.
seams.leakage: Chat attestations remain Slack-specific, operator and adapter principals are limited to explicit-user sets, adapters can reach only approvals routed to bindings they serve, and Console principals cannot assert channel evidence.
seams.nextStep: Exercise the adapter principal with another real interactive channel without widening any existing principal kind or accepting the platform key as resolver identity.

seams.label: Workflow state store
seams.implementations: 1 state API router over Postgres JSONB
seams.contract: Scoped namespace/key document API with size limits, CAS behavior, and singular shared NULL-scope identity
seams.reason: The HTTP state router is useful, but not every state consumer stays behind it; operator memory and relational paths can bypass the supposed boundary.
seams.leakage: A second state backend would not cover direct model/JSONB access, while memory and transcript loaders still depend on the HTTP shape and capacity limits.
seams.nextStep: Inventory and close bypasses before extracting another backend; then treat retention, capacity, and back-pressure as one admission policy.

seams.label: Agent memory
seams.implementations: 1 real loader (StateApiMemoryStore)
seams.contract: MemoryStore load/append, optional replace, and boot-preamble injection over a scoped state token
seams.reason: The loader port and null implementation are clean, but no alternate durable memory backend has exercised them.
seams.leakage: The operator inspect/seed/edit/delete plane addresses the Postgres WorkflowStateEntry backing directly instead of going through MemoryStore.
seams.nextStep: Keep the operator plane and any future loader consistent before adding another backing; automatic learned-record extraction remains future work.

seams.label: Conversation history
seams.implementations: 1 real loader (StateApiTranscriptStore)
seams.contract: TranscriptStore load/append of portable structured turn and summary records, scoped by agent and thread
seams.reason: One real state API store supports structured replay, tool result continuity, bounded compaction, optional native checkpoint reuse, and versioned capacity recovery. Appends reserve space for publication outcomes; on 413 the store rewrites a compacted value by compare-and-set, preserves publication markers and the newest turn, reloads on conflict, and retries before returning a classified terminal failure.
seams.leakage: Compaction deliberately replaces older message and tool detail with a bounded summary and drops the old native checkpoint. State value and namespace caps still apply, and a value that cannot fit its publication markers, summary, newest turn, and reserve requires operator recovery through versioned export and delete. Ordinary persistence failure marks durability lost, preventing safe cold handoff.
seams.nextStep: Keep portable replay authoritative, preserve publication outcomes under pressure, and make any future source retention policy explicit.

seams.label: Trigger ingestion
seams.implementations: 7 distinct ingress paths: Slack, GitHub push, GitHub review, signed GitHub factory issue events, commit polling, named HMAC hooks, and worker cron slots
seams.contract: No unified runtime trigger port. Factory issue ingress verifies GitHub authority and records a canonical WorkItem; cron claims one SQL slot and enqueues a bounded turn; generic hooks and reviews keep their existing distinct checks.
seams.reason: Several triggers now run, including factory issues and cron, but they do not implement one shared trigger interface or event lifecycle.
seams.leakage: Slack enters through dispatcher; GitHub push, review, factory issues, polling, and generic hooks enter through API handlers; cron starts in the worker. Review feedback and factory work have their own durable admission and outbox rules. Bundle declared generic hook installation remains planned.
seams.nextStep: Reconcile the shipped cron and factory paths with the trigger interface before adding another trigger kind.

seams.label: Agent-facing CLI output
seams.implementations: 48 typed outputs behind one trait across many verbs
seams.contract: CliOutput + Ui.emit + versioned JSON result schemas
seams.reason: Many independent command results exercise the same human/JSON emission boundary.
seams.leakage: A tracked set of legacy/operator verbs still has inline or unstructured success output.
seams.nextStep: Finish migrating the tracked exceptions without widening the output contract.

seams.label: MCP connector host
seams.implementations: 1 real Kubernetes host + in-memory fake
seams.contract: Bundle declaration → rendered workload → bounded rollout readiness → mounted MCP entry → runner capability probe
seams.reason: The lifecycle now observes rollout and runner capability outcomes, and transient probe failures can recover on later turns. The renderer and CLI share frozen vectors for the derived Bearer rule, accepting an explicit bearer_secret or one plain-string secret while excluding an implicit SecretRef. The typed client still exposes raw Kubernetes JSON, rendering remains Kubernetes specific outside the port, and CLI and reconciler paths do not share identical apply and prune semantics.
seams.leakage: Build inputs, pinned images, delegated OAuth, runtime injection, reconciliation, and Kubernetes objects cross control plane and cluster ownership. Only one real host sits behind the port. Skill and local tiers use a separate Docker applier with its own label, pruning, and readiness wait outside this interface.
seams.nextStep: Close runtime injection and converge CLI/reconciler lifecycle before calling the host portable.

seams.label: MCP service-key authentication
seams.implementations: 1 deployment-owned service identity mode
seams.contract: Named hosted Bearer secret → derived placeholder → cluster-scoped sandbox bind → in-memory expansion → environment name removal
seams.reason: Service credentials cross a named secret boundary, expand into the MCP header in memory, and are removed from the runner process environment before turns, but no second production identity mode has proved the abstraction.
seams.leakage: Secret rendering and delivery still span bundle declaration, API, Kubernetes, kubelet and container environment exposure before process startup, and SecretRef residuals.
seams.nextStep: Keep service authentication explicit and fail closed; prove delegated OAuth as a separate identity mode with no fallback between them.

seams.label: Per-person MCP OAuth
seams.implementations: 0; accepted architecture only
seams.contract: Canonical run principal → principal-scoped grant → control-plane-owned OAuth gateway → MCP server
seams.reason: ADR-0088 defines the ownership and fail-closed behavior, but the gateway, grant lifecycle, connection action, and resume path are not shipped.
seams.leakage: Until implemented, MCP calls cannot safely act with each human's authority; the existing deployment service identity is the only current mode.
seams.nextStep: Implement discovery, PKCE, encrypted grant storage, refresh and revocation, then prove missing-auth pause and post-callback resume without giving the runner a raw token.

seams.label: Sealed connector credential
seams.implementations: 1 cross-language wire (Rust sealer, Python opener)
seams.contract: Frozen sealed-credential envelope with cluster-side opening
seams.reason: The Rust sealer and Python opener interoperate, but the product path is disconnected: validation and delivery do not yet form one working production consumer path.
seams.leakage: Security depends on exact agreement between CLI, API rendering, cluster delivery, and the currently uncalled opener.
seams.nextStep: Connect and prove the complete sealed-secret path before expanding its wire or consumers.

seams.label: Bundle / plugin format
seams.implementations: 1 deliberately adopted format (Claude Code plugin)
seams.contract: Frozen Pydantic models including unhosted_url, SecretRef, and bearer_secret, plus regenerated committed JSON Schema and an immutable content-addressed bundle. The exact platform publication tool mcp__curie__publish_changes is a recognized approval gate without requiring a declared external MCP server. Bundle tool policy cannot remove Curie's built-in platform MCP tools, while a bundle-mounted server named curie remains fully in scope.
seams.reason: The format is strongly enforced but intentionally has one implementation and one ecosystem shape.
seams.leakage: This is the main coupling that a non-Claude harness must interpret or translate.
seams.nextStep: Do not invent another format; require alternate harnesses to demonstrate a translation strategy.

seams.label: Third-party port adapter
seams.implementations: 0 generic adapter-kit services; Discord and email are first-party adapters on the shipped HTTP edge
seams.contract: Intended deployed-service placement with a shipped scoped adapter credential; generic packaging and conformance remain unbuilt
seams.reason: ADR-0096 places a third-party adapter as a deployed service, and ADR-0154 now supplies a scoped runtime principal for channel token rotation plus approval listing and resolution. The generic kit is still unbuilt; first-party Discord and email adapters use the HTTP edge without that kit.
seams.leakage: Adapter discovery, installation, routing, conformance, and lifecycle are still future work. The scoped credential is a prerequisite, not a complete third-party adapter product.
seams.nextStep: Build the adapter kit only if a third-party channel needs install, discovery, and conformance beyond the two shipped first-party adapters.

seams.label: Agent Proxy boundary
seams.contract: Accepted credential and egress enforcement boundary outside the sandbox
seams.reason: The direction is accepted but intentionally unimplemented pending narrower substrate, TLS, and injection decisions.
seams.leakage: Provider credentials and web egress still enter the sandbox under current controls.
seams.nextStep: Land the follow-up ADRs for substrate, TLS termination, and credential injection before implementation.

seams.label: Eval result → promotion authority
seams.implementations: Commit status exists; internal promotion enforcement does not
seams.contract: Reserved policy boundary between graded evidence and production deployment
seams.reason: The API reports eval state to GitHub, but process_push does not read that result before creating a production deployment.
seams.leakage: Safety depends on external branch protection and release policy rather than a product invariant.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance first, then bind promotion to an authoritative graded result without rebuilding the artifact.
